description: Samoa's Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) publishes a water resources dashboard on its e-government dashboard portal, next to dashboards for forestry, climate change, waste, communications and the meteorology office. Read on 27 September 2026, it shows water catchments, hydro monitoring stations, groundwater springs and the stream network with a monitoring station registry: 54 monitoring stations (49 operational, 5 not operational, 37 with telemetry) in categories groundwater borehole, isotope sampler, rain gauge and water level. Map layers list 65 water catchments with areas, 33 hydro stations (20 boreholes, 11 water level, 2 rainfall samplers), 24 groundwater springs (developed, natural and village springs on Upolu) and 486 streams from the integrated watershed management programme. Coverage is Samoa. Access is online and free; tables can be exported as CSV or PDF, and the map uses Esri World Imagery. Caveats: the dashboard sits in a GEF project portfolio portal with a login option, and no licence is stated. Simulation uses: catchment, spring and station inventories for water supply source mapping and flood and drought monitoring on small islands. Related records: HydroSHEDS (data-hydrosheds-hydrorivers-hydrobasins) and WPdx (data-wpdx-water-point-data-exchange).
